The rescue, non-repelling force, culpable agents, and selective will are all present in the focus wording; the preceding sudden-punishment warning supplies a distinct macro trigger, and all five supports are retained.

All eight trace roles have supplied root and word-index contacts at 12:94, 12:96, or the focus and return through focus words 12:110:9 and 12:110:15. The restoration sequence is retained as attributed analogy, bounded by the connection note that 12:96 is not itself the focus's aid-and-force structure.

The ten trace roles connect shelter and security, a realized earlier sign, release from confinement, subtlety, and willing to the focus arrival. They support a qualified culmination reading while leaving open that aid may begin as a discrete intervention at arrival.

The six trace roles at 12:101 place the prayer for faithful death and joining to the righteous after worldly attainment. They widen the possible endpoint of rescue without making death the focus's lexical meaning or defining the criterion of selection.

The eight trace roles connect the focus's uncertain inference and falsity attribution with concealed transmission, visible signs passed over, turning aside, and divided belief. The relation is retained as attributed context, not as a claim that later audiences caused the messengers' crisis.

The eight trace roles join 12:107's sudden, enveloping warning to the focus's arrival, selective rescue, and non-repelling force. This survives as an attributed structural analogy; the packet does not establish that both ayat describe the same event.

All eight trace roles land at 12:109's sent messengers, embodied men, settlements, travel, observation, outcome, and reasoning, and return to the focus messengers and their crisis. The historical method is attributed to later hearers rather than assigned to the messengers themselves.

The eight trace roles at 12:111 connect the focus's falsity attribution and arrival to story, reflection, non-fabrication, confirmation, detail, and guidance. The explicit closing relation and its connection record support a retrospective verification reading while the pronoun direction remains unresolved.

findings.title: Despair within a history of reception
findings.claim: The severed hope and feared falsity remain the messengers' lived crisis, while 12:103-111 places it among audiences that fail to receive signs and are then asked to inspect historical outcomes. The close makes this threshold part of a longer problem of reception and retrospective reading, rather than an isolated interval.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries severed expectation through uncertain thought to perceived falsity and arriving aid. The pericope says most do not believe despite the addressee's keenness (12:103), describes people passing visible signs while turning aside and belief mixed with association (12:105-106), then asks hearers to inspect prior outcomes (12:109) and calls the stories instructive and confirming (12:111). Those surrounding acts change the focus crisis into a threshold held within both failed reception and a method of later reading.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the extremity of the messengers' expectation without losing the longer frame in which apparent delay and rejection are examined through outcomes.
findings.containment: The verses about later audiences do not say that those audiences caused the messengers' thought. The finding does not resolve the direction or force of the wording at كُذِبُوا۟; it keeps the stated crisis intact and adds the pericope's retrospective frame.

epistemic.reason: The channel supports are trusted, focus branches are registered, and the cited context surfaces directly state nonbelief, ignored signs, historical inspection, and the stories' instructive role.

findings.title: Rescue within an unrelaxed warning
findings.claim: After 12:107 asks whether people feel secure from a sudden enveloping punishment or the Hour, 12:110 distinguishes those rescued by divine will from criminals against whom force is not turned back. The macro sequence makes rescue a selective exit, not a blanket suspension of consequence.
findings.mechanism: The focus coordinates the passive rescue of chosen persons with the negated repelling of force from culpable people. The preceding warning supplies sudden coming, an enveloping event, and punishment; it changes the pair of focus clauses into the outcome side of an unresolved warning rather than a general promise of safety.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold deliverance and judgment in one field: rescue is real and selective, while the warning's force remains in view.
findings.containment: No identity between the warning in 12:107 and the event in 12:110 is asserted. The focus still states aid and rescue plainly; the contextual warning adds the limit that rescue is not universal immunity.

epistemic.reason: The trusted channel evidence matches the focus clauses, and 12:107 explicitly supplies sudden coming and punishment as the independent macro trigger.

findings.title: A sign already in motion
findings.claim: The 12:94-96 sequence makes the focus's arrival compatible with an earlier carrier phase: the caravan departs, scent makes Yusuf's absence perceptible, then a bearer arrives and sight returns. The focus's aid can therefore be read as public verification of a sign already moving, rather than necessarily as an intervention with no perceptual precursor.
findings.mechanism: The focus arrival at 12:110:9 meets a pericope sequence of departure, scent, a bearer, arrival, return, and restored sight. The focus's phrase that force is not turned away also meets the earlier return to sight: beneficial restoration and non-reversal of force remain distinct outcomes within the same story.
findings.reader_payoff: The threshold of aid can feel abrupt to those inside the crisis while the larger narrative lets a reader notice a faint sign-chain before its public arrival.
findings.containment: The 12:96 episode is a family restoration, and the supplied connection note explicitly limits it as not the focus's aid-and-force structure. This is an attributed structural analogy, not a claim that the messengers received the same precursor or that divine aid always works by this mechanism.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus and context root coordinates are supplied and match their occurrence summaries, but the reconstructed HFT interpretation is unbound and remains attributed.

findings.title: Arrival as the end of a long reordering
findings.claim: The reunion and retrospective account in 12:99-100 make visible arrival in 12:110 readable as the threshold at which a long, fine-grained reordering becomes legible. The threshold can remain abrupt to those within it even when the narrative has already shown shelter, security, an old sign coming true, and release from confinement.
findings.mechanism: The focus names arrival and aid. Before it, 12:99 gathers the family into shelter and security; 12:100 joins an old vision to its realized outcome, release from prison, and a process described as subtle in what is willed. These contextual carriers meet the focus arrival and selective agency, changing the reader's temporal scale from aid beginning visibly at arrival to arrival disclosing a longer trajectory.
findings.reader_payoff: A sudden threshold can still feel sudden while the reader recognizes the longer sequence that the story has already allowed to unfold.
findings.containment: The context does not prove that 12:110's aid began earlier or disclose a hidden causal mechanism. A discrete intervention at the focus threshold remains a live reading.

epistemic.reason: The anchor roots and word indices match supplied context occurrences, but the claim that arrival culminates an already active process is a reconstructed, unbound HFT inference.

findings.title: Rescue and a farther endpoint
findings.claim: After recounting worldly attainment, Yusuf asks to be taken in submission and joined to the righteous. Beside that prayer, the focus's selective rescue can include faithful completion and belonging as a possible endpoint, while worldly survival remains a real form of deliverance.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries rescue through separation and names those selected by will. In 12:101 the contextual speaker, after receiving authority and knowledge, asks for death in submission and to be joined to the sound; these distinct acts contact the focus's rescue and selection, widening its possible endpoint beyond continued worldly life.
findings.reader_payoff: Rescue can be perceived as release into right belonging as well as escape from immediate danger.
findings.containment: The prayer is Yusuf's and does not define the focus's verb, disclose the criterion of selection, or say that the messengers died. The focus's immediate rescue remains intact.

epistemic.reason: The contextual prayer and focus words are exact packet evidence; the extension from Yusuf's stated desire to a possible endpoint of rescue is the unbound HFT's attributed inference.

findings.title: A crisis inside competing modes of reception
findings.claim: The focus's uncertain thought and feared falsity sit after a report transmitted from the unseen and beside visible signs that people pass while turning away, followed by belief mixed with association. The pericope thus places the crisis within a wider field where hidden communication, visible evidence, and partial reception do not guarantee recognition.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries uncertain inference and an attribution of falsity. In 12:102 knowledge is revealed despite ordinary absence; in 12:105 manifest signs are repeatedly passed and turned away from; 12:106 describes belief accompanied by association. These differing reception states contact the focus's doubt and perceived falsity, changing the frame from a private interval alone to a pericope-wide problem of how evidence is received.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see that visibility and communication are both present in the surrounding account, yet recognition remains unsettled.
findings.containment: The verses about audiences indict those audiences; they do not state that those people caused the messengers' thought. The relation is a macro context for the crisis, not a diagnosis of the messengers or a claim that the message failed.

epistemic.reason: The roots and word positions align with supplied context occurrences, while the interpretation that they form one reception ecology comes from an unbound reconstructed HFT trace.

findings.title: One threshold, asymmetric outcomes
findings.claim: The sudden, enveloping warning in 12:107 supplies an event-shape for the focus's threshold: one position is described through extraction into safety, another through force that cannot be turned away. Read as an attributed analogy, the focus's aid and force can be perceived as asymmetric outcomes in one field.
findings.mechanism: The focus joins arrival, rescue, and non-repelling force. The preceding verse repeats the coming of an enveloping punishment or the Hour, then marks its suddenness and the audience's failure to perceive. Those independent cues contact the focus's paired outcomes and make the threshold feel sudden and asymmetrically experienced.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive rescue without letting it erase the warning's force, and can perceive suddenness without treating the warning as an event already identified with the focus.
findings.containment: 12:107 names alternatives and may concern a separate future event. Its relation to 12:110 is an event-shape analogy only; it does not establish identity, timing, or a general rule about judgment.

epistemic.reason: The supplied roots and coordinates align, but the shared-threshold interpretation is explicitly an unbound HFT inference and retains the separate-event alternative.

findings.title: Messengers in an inspectable human history
findings.claim: 12:109 places messengers among embodied men sent to settlements, then asks later hearers to travel, observe prior outcomes, and reason from them. This changes the focus from an exceptional private interval alone to pressure within public human transmission across time, where the middle of a process is not the whole evidence.
findings.mechanism: The focus names messengers at the point of severed hope and perceived falsity. The preceding verse describes sent men receiving revelation and directs hearers toward travel, sight, outcomes, and reasoning. Those contextual acts contact the focus's messengers and crisis, changing the temporal scale from an isolated wait to a history that later observers are asked to inspect.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold human vulnerability and prophetic transmission together, then see why the text directs later hearers to completed outcomes rather than judging only from delay.
findings.containment: 12:109 does not say that the travel command corrects the messengers' own experience or that they had access to later evidence. It offers a method to later hearers; the focus's despair and arriving aid remain intact.

epistemic.reason: The focus and context root coordinates match supplied occurrences. The macro interpretation joining them is a reconstructed HFT reading from an unbound source and is kept attributed.

findings.title: Arrival as an evidentiary hinge
findings.claim: 12:111 calls the stories instructive, not fabricated, confirming, detailed, and guiding. Immediately after the focus's attribution of falsity and arrival of aid, that close makes the rescue an evidentiary hinge inside a narrated trace, preserving how convincing the apparent falsity felt before the outcome.
findings.mechanism: The focus moves from perceived falsity to arrival. The closing verse names story-following, reflection, non-fabrication, confirmation, detail, and guidance; those operations contact the focus's disputed verdict and arrival, changing rescue from an event that merely ends danger into an outcome that can be read retrospectively within the story.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can keep the crisis's felt uncertainty and still see why the narrative asks for a later, detailed reading of outcomes.
findings.containment: The closing verse validates the narrated account but does not settle the exact pronoun direction in كُذِبُوا۟ or prove which interpretation of that phrase the messengers held. Rescue remains an event as well as a point in the narrative's verification frame.

epistemic.reason: 12:111's surface and word coordinates are supplied, as is a directly relevant connection row, but the evidentiary-hinge reading is an unbound HFT interpretation.

findings.title: Requested aid beside aid arriving
findings.claim: Fātiḥa 1:5 asks God for aid, while 12:110 narrates aid arriving to messengers after hope has ended. Beside that direct request, the focus's arrival can be heard as a narrated instance of the aid invoked in the external prayer.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries نَصْرُ as aid arriving to the messengers; 1:5 supplies the independent plural request نَسْتَعِينُ. Their contact shifts aid from an abstract object of supplication to a narrated act within the story, without asserting that the messengers themselves made this prayer.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold the present plea for help beside a narrated arrival of help at a threshold of despair.
findings.containment: The two verses do not state that the messengers prayed this wording or that every plea receives the same outcome. This is a bounded overlay from the explicitly supplied external ayah.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies both exact surfaces and a direct aid-to-aid contact; the overlay supports a parallel between request and narrated arrival, not a causal or guaranteed response.
